representation_fit.evidence: Brief asks for explore over high-dimensionality, high-density data (brief.md shape bundle); initial screen is a purpose-built dimensional explorer: scatter projection with four swappable encoding slots (X/Y/Color/Size) over 10 typed dimensions (screenshots/1280x860.png; source/data.js:67-79; source/app.js:19,149-156), plus per-dimension filter rail and record table — dimensions themselves are the primary navigable objects, matching the dimensional-space shape.

primary_task_salience.evidence: Exploration surface dominates: chart fills the center of both viewports with 1,204 points plotted at first paint (screenshots/1280x860.png, 1440x900.png), encoding-slot controls sit top-left (source/index.html:30-36), filter bar and dimension rail are one interaction away; no competing task chrome.

time_to_understand.evidence: Model-judged proxy on initial screen: header names the artifact and mode 'AURORA Exoplanet Catalog / Dimensional Explorer' (source/index.html:15-16); scope line '1,204 / 1,204 in scope · 0 selected' states state at a glance; axis titles embed dimension+scale 'Planet Radius (R⊕) · lin' / 'Orbital Period (days) · log' (source/app.js:349-351, visible in both screenshots); empty states instruct ('No active filters — add them from the dimension rail', Inspector 'Select a record…'). Caveat: 10–11.5px type slows reading (source/styles.css:22,181,186).

navigation_cost.evidence: Single screen, zero mode changes: any dimension switch is one select change (source/app.js:92-100), filters are one details-row expansion in the always-visible rail (source/app.js:177-184), record detail is one click in chart or table (source/app.js:493-504,512-529); revert controls (undo/reset/clear) permanently in header (source/index.html:21-24). No routes, dialogs, or drill-downs required.

context_loss.evidence: Structure encodes the brief's success criterion 'dimension switching does not reset cognition': selection and inspector bind to record id, not projection (source/app.js:26-27,423-449; self-test T2 'selection survives dimension switch' source/app.js:640-642); table scroll position and row focus restored across re-render (source/app.js:382-419); projection has a per-step undo stack (source/app.js:91,101-105; T5/T6 source/app.js:671-687); inspector text states 'The profile follows the record, not the current projection' (source/index.html:63, visible in both screenshots).

ui_surface_complexity.evidence: Permanent surfaces: header with 4 revert buttons (source/index.html:20-25), 4 slot selects + 2 scale toggles + 10 always-expanded dimension rows in the rail (screenshots/1280x860.png; source/app.js:159-185), filter bar, legend, 5-column table, inspector. Every surface has a distinct job for a 10-dimension dataset, but the permanently rendered 10-row rail plus four global buttons is near the heavy end; no redundant or decorative chrome observed.

accessibility.evidence: Receipt fails all four a11y/type checks: a11y.contrast, a11y.focus_order, a11y.target_size, type.min_projected_size (measurement-summary.json:13-16); consistent with 10–11.5px body/table/hint type (source/styles.css:22,181,186,96) and faint #5b6572 hint text (source/styles.css:9). Mitigating source effort exists — :focus-visible outlines (source/styles.css:50-53), aria-labels on generated controls (source/app.js:154,166-167), keyboard-operable rows with Enter/arrows (source/app.js:531-541), visually-hidden chart description (source/index.html:47) — but the measured outcomes fail, so affordance quality cannot offset them.

frontend_rework.evidence: Visible defect at both viewports: record table's 4th column header 'STELL…' clipped mid-word at the right panel edge and 5th column (Planet Mass) entirely off-view at initial state (screenshots/1280x860.png and 1440x900.png right panel), caused by nowrap table cells in a fixed 296px column (source/styles.css:165-187); matches receipt layout.overflow=fail and layout.responsive_collision=fail; 6 of 7 checks fail overall (measurement-summary.json:4-7,13-16) implying rework; text.truncation=pass and target_invalid=false are the mitigating signals.

acceptance_seed_coverage.evidence: Seed 'filter/projection state has ownership and is revertible' is addressed explicitly: one owner per dimension in state (source/app.js:25), rail rows show filter dot + active summary per dimension (source/app.js:140-146), controls literally labeled 'Range filter (owner: …)' (source/app.js:163) and chips titled 'Owner dimension: …' with individual × removal (source/app.js:264-266; T4 'removes exactly one filter' source/app.js:663-669), per-dimension 'Remove X filter' link (source/app.js:183,237-250), projection undo/reset per-step (source/app.js:91,106-111; T5/T6 source/app.js:671-687).

defects_observed: Record table overflows its 296px panel at both viewports: 'Stellar Class' header clipped to 'STELL' mid-word and 'Planet Mass' column invisible without horizontal scroll (screenshots/1280x860.png, 1440x900.png; layout.overflow + layout.responsive_collision fail)
6 of 7 automated checks fail: layout.overflow, layout.responsive_collision, a11y.contrast, a11y.focus_order, a11y.target_size, type.min_projected_size (measurement-summary.json:13-16)
Type sizes below comfortable minimums in places (10–11.5px hints, legend, table cells; source/styles.css:73,96,136,181,186), consistent with type.min_projected_size fail
At 1280 the Records column header hint 'Enter selects · ↑↓ move' wraps onto its own line (screenshots/1280x860.png), a minor responsive-collision symptom
scores.overall_note: This package is a structurally excellent answer to the brief's cognitive job: a single-screen dimensional explorer where 10 typed dimensions feed four swappable encoding slots over 1,204 first-paint-ready records, with selection and inspector keyed to record identity so re-projection never resets context (source/app.js:26-27, T2), and filter/projection state carrying explicit ownership and per-item revert — the acceptance seed is covered in both source and UI language (owner labels, chips, undo stack, T3–T6). The weaknesses are all surface-quality: the fixed-width record table clips its fourth column and hides its fifth at both tested viewports, and the receipt fails six of seven checks including every accessibility and type-size check, despite genuine a11y effort visible in the source (focus-visible styles, aria-labels, keyboard table navigation). Net: strong representation, navigation, context preservation, and seed coverage; material deductions for layout overflow and measured accessibility failures. Human preference, task time, and retrieval accuracy remain unobservable in this blind pilot; model judgment here is not human preference.
